structure: Part 6, Place of destination and consignor pickers. Read in full: the shared address-book-picker folder (address-lines.js, render.js, pagination.js, view-model.js); every file of features/place-of-destination (page.js, evaluation.js, fields.js, controller.js, template.njk, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, view-model/index.js, view-model/pagination.js, place-of-destination.fit.spec.js); the same set for features/consignor-select; and obligations/sections/destination.js. For page size, captions and task-row titles the pages refer to, services/address-book/index.js (PAGE_SIZE and its header comments), flow/section-captions/copy/copy.en.js and hub/copy/copy.en.js were looked up by line, not read in full. Layout: the two pages are near-identical address-book pickers built on one shared surface (search box, one page of results as small radios in a table with a View details disclosure, an inset for the current selection, govukPagination, the shared save actions). Place of destination (/notifications/{ref}/destinations/select) asks one of three questions chosen from commodity type and arrival status; consignor (/notifications/{ref}/consignors/select) asks one question and redirects to the overview when the consignor is out of scope. Both store only an address-book id. destination.js holds one obligation, placeOfDestination; the consignor obligation lives in obligations/sections/parties.js, outside this part, and only its binding is claimed here. Claims run: shared picker behaviour (001-020), place of destination page (021-052), consignor page (053-066), obligations and bindings (067-069), then every fit test in place-of-destination.fit.spec.js (070-088) and consignor-select.fit.spec.js (089-109), then gaps (110-111).

claims.statement: Each address-book picker row shows the address as one line made of address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and postal or zip code, in that order, joined with commas, skipping empty parts and leaving the country out because it has its own column.
claims.quote:
const ADDRESS_PARTS = [
  'addressLine1',
  'addressLine2',
  'townOrCity',
  'county',
  'postalOrZipCode'
]

/** The address as one line for the results table. The country has its own
 * column, so it is left out here. */
export const addressText = (address = {}) =>
  ADDRESS_PARTS.map((part) => address[part])
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(', ')

claims.statement: A picker row's View details disclosure lists everything the record holds, one line each: the name, each address part, the country, the telephone number and the email address, skipping any that are empty.

A picker selection counts only if the address book still holds that record: a missing or soft-deleted id is treated as no selection, the same as a stored reference to a deleted record reading as never entered.
claims.quote:
A selection resolves only to a record the book still holds: a missing or
 * soft-deleted id is treated as no selection, the same way a stored reference
 * to a deleted record reads as never entered.

claims.statement: When the address book is unavailable the picker does not treat it as a deleted selection: the failure propagates as an error, so an outage is never indistinguishable from a deletion.
claims.quote:
An outage is not that — the
 * address book throws and the throw propagates, because an unavailable service
 * must never be indistinguishable from a deletion.

claims.statement: A selected id that no longer resolves to a record is not shown as the selected address and is not carried in the paging links.

claims.statement: Picker paging is a plain link, not a form submit, and each page link carries the search term (q), the page number (page) and the currently ticked address (selected) in its query string, so a row ticked on one page is not lost on paging.
claims.quote:
Paging is a link, not a submit, so everything the next page needs travels
 * in the query string: the search term, the page and the row the trader has
 * already ticked. Without the selection a trader who picks a row on page one
 * and then pages loses it.

claims.statement: Picker pagination shows a Previous link on every page after the first and a Next link on every page before the last, labelled from the page's own copy so they read in the page's language rather than govukPagination's built-in English.

`labels`, the resolved `previous` and `next`

claims.statement: The first results row on every page takes the field name as its radio id, so the error summary link always moves focus to the first row; later rows are numbered by their position in the whole result set so ids stay distinct across pages.

 * so ids stay distinct across pages.

claims.statement: Neither picker page offers a link to add a new address or to manage the address book: the templates hold only search, results, paging and the save actions, so a trader whose address is missing has no way forward from the page itself.
